evals.name: velocity-reference-map-full
evals.prompt: Validate the VeloCity reference context map (docs/domains/velocity/velocity-context-map.md and the CML) with residuality theory. I'm the trainer, not a participant, so the spoiler doesn't matter. Throw lots of different stressors at it and tell me where it breaks and what you'd change.
evals.expected_output: analysis.json + analysis.md under docs/residuality/velocity/...; 25-40 concrete stressors across all categories incl. absurd; attractors reused across stressors; incidence matrix from the script with hidden-coupling candidates; augmented architecture traced to attractors; independent test set with Ri computed; CML and map untouched.
assertions: analysis.json and analysis.md both created
analysis.json passes residuality_matrix.py validation (exit code 0)
At least 25 non-withdrawn training stressors
Stressors span at least 7 distinct categories, including an absurd one
Fewer attractors than half the number of stressors (attractors are reused)
Every stressor has a naive verdict with a reason and a residue
Report contains an incidence matrix with column totals
Report names at least one hidden coupling (co-impact pair without a direct relationship)
Residual architecture changes reference both stressors and attractors
Separate test stressor set (>=10) with naive and residual verdicts
Residual index Ri reported with its arithmetic
CML and velocity-context-map.md not modified

evals.name: rentals-single-context-user-stressors
evals.prompt: how robust is our Rentals bounded context really? I'm worried about two things in particular: the city might start requiring every ride to end in a geofenced bay with photo proof, and we might add e-bikes that need charging. stress-test rentals with those plus whatever else you come up with
evals.expected_output: Scope is the Rentals context code (aggregates, ports, adapters) plus its neighbours; the two user stressors are included and tagged source=user; 15-25 stressors; matrix over Rentals components; residues at the code/boundary level; no code changes; offers follow-up via other skills.
assertions: analysis.json and analysis.md both created
Components include Rentals-internal elements (e.g. BikeStation aggregate, BikeStationRepo, RentBikeUseCase)
Both user stressors (geofenced bay/photo, e-bike charging) present and marked as from the user
Between 15 and 30 training stressors
Report contains an incidence matrix with column totals
Residual index Ri reported with its arithmetic
No Java source files modified

evals.name: crowdsorcery-poke-holes
evals.prompt: poke holes in the CrowdSorcery architecture - which bounded contexts would fall over first if the business environment shifted? I want something I can show the group tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: Reads CrowdSorcery.md, the crowdsorcery packages and the in-code context map; builds the naive architecture from them; stressor analysis with attractors; matrix; ranked hot spots answering 'which falls over first'; augmented architecture; Ri; report saved under docs/residuality/crowdsorcery/....
assertions: analysis.json and analysis.md both created
Components include the CrowdSorcery contexts found in code (e.g. deposit, investment, payment, fundraising)
At least 20 non-withdrawn training stressors
Report ranks components by impact (answers which falls over first)
Report contains an incidence matrix with column totals
Residual index Ri reported with its arithmetic
